br.heroDesc1: Large, heavy breasts can cause more than aesthetic concerns. Many patients experience chronic neck, shoulder, and back pain, posture strain, bra-strap grooving, skin irritation under the breast fold, and difficulty exercising or finding comfortable clothing. Clinical guidance from the UK NHS recognises breast reduction surgery as a treatment option when large breasts contribute to ongoing physical discomfort and daily functional limitation.
br.heroDesc2: At Dr. Soma Plastic Surgery, every breast reduction procedure is performed by Dr. Soma, a board-certified plastic surgeon with extensive experience in aesthetic and functional breast surgery. The goal is not simply to "make breasts smaller" but to achieve a balanced size, improved symmetry, healthier nipple position, and long-term comfort using careful planning and safety-focused technique.
br.whatIsDesc1: Breast reduction, or <highlight>reduction mammaplasty</highlight>, is a surgical procedure that reduces breast size by removing excess breast tissue, fat, and stretched skin, while reshaping and lifting the breast for a natural appearance.
br.whatIsDesc2: It is both a functional and aesthetic procedure. The goal is not simply to "make breasts smaller" but to achieve a balanced size, improved symmetry, and a healthier nipple position.
br.reliefDesc: Alleviates chronic neck, shoulder, and back strain.
br.proportionDesc: Creates a size that balances with your body frame.
br.reason1Desc: Rashes or infections under the breast fold.
br.reason2Desc: Bra-strap grooving and difficulty finding clothes.
br.howDesc: Dr. Soma focuses on proportion, stability, and long-term contour, rather than an overly flat or unnatural reduction.
br.step0Desc: Detailed measurements, symmetry planning, and marking the incision pattern.
br.step1Desc: Removing excess heavy tissue, fat, and skin to reduce volume and weight.
br.step2Desc: Lifting remaining tissue for firmness and repositioning the nipple naturally.
br.step3Desc: Layered closure for support, followed by dressings and a surgical bra.
br.typesDesc: Technique selection depends on breast size, degree of sagging, and desired final proportion.
br.type0Desc: Most common. Removes tissue and excess skin while lifting the breast. Repositions the nipple to a natural height for a lighter, balanced contour.
br.type1Desc: For patients with significant heaviness and discomfort. Involves greater tissue removal and stronger internal support. Prioritizes daily comfort.
br.type2Desc: For patients with stretched, enlarged areolas. Reduces areola diameter to match the new breast size, enhancing overall symmetry and aesthetic.
br.rec0Desc: Support bra applied. Mild to moderate soreness. Walking encouraged immediately. Rest and avoid lifting.
br.rec1Desc: Return to desk work for many. Bruising improves. Light walking continues. Support bra essential.
br.rec2Desc: Resume light exercise with approval. Improved posture and comfort noticeable. Shape continues settling.
br.rec3Desc: Final contour becomes natural. Scars soften and fade. Long-term comfort benefits clear.
br.painDesc: "Tightness and soreness similar to a deep chest workout." - Discomfort is manageable with medication.
br.cand0: Large or heavy breasts causing discomfort.
br.cand1: Chronic back, neck, or shoulder strain.
br.cand2: Skin irritation or rashes under breasts.
br.cand4: Non-smoker or willing to stop temporarily.
br.notSuitableDesc: Pregnant/breastfeeding, uncontrolled medical conditions, planning major weight loss, or smoking without willingness to stop.
br.ben0: Reduces neck, shoulder, and back pain
br.ben3: Creates a lighter, more proportionate size
br.ben4: Reduces bra-strap grooving and improves fit

br.faqDesc: Clear answers to help you make informed decisions
br.faq0A: Breast reduction is a surgical procedure that reduces breast size by removing excess breast tissue, fat, and skin, while reshaping and lifting the breast for a lighter, more proportionate result.
br.faq1A: Incisions are planned based on breast size and sagging. Excess tissue and skin are removed, the breast is reshaped, and the nipple and areola are repositioned to a higher, natural level.
br.faq2Q: When will I see results after breast reduction?
br.faq2A: You will notice immediate reduction in size, but swelling takes time to settle. Many patients feel more comfortable within 2–4 weeks, with final contour refining over 3–6 months.
br.faq3Q: Will breast reduction remove back and shoulder pain?
br.faq3A: Many patients report significant improvement in neck, shoulder, and back discomfort after surgery, especially when symptoms are caused by breast heaviness.
br.faq4A: Discomfort is usually mild to moderate in the first week and is controlled with medication. Most patients describe soreness and tightness rather than sharp pain.
br.faq5Q: Can I breastfeed after breast reduction?
br.faq5A: Breastfeeding may still be possible, but it can be affected depending on the technique and tissue removed. This is discussed during consultation based on your future plans.
br.faq6A: Yes. Scars depend on the technique required. They are placed strategically and usually fade significantly over time with proper scar care.
br.faq7Q: How much smaller will my breasts be?
br.faq7A: The target size is planned around your body frame, tissue quality, and goals. The safest and most proportionate reduction is chosen, not an arbitrary cup size.
